title: Cardinal enlargement for a small family of arrows
statement: Use universes, accessibility and compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category and $S$ a small set of its arrows. There exist infinite regular cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ in the smaller universe such that $\kappa$ is uncountable, $\mathcal C$ is both $\lambda$-accessible and $\kappa$-accessible, and $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for every pair of cardinals $\mu<\kappa$ and $\nu<\lambda$. Both endpoints of every arrow in $S$ are $\kappa$-compact. The full subcategory $\mathcal C^\kappa$ of all $\kappa$-compact objects is essentially small.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.2(2), Proposition 5.4.2.9 and Corollary 5.3.4.15; the cardinal choice in Lemma 5.5.4.14 (3)⇒(1), p. 480, enlarged as in the proof of Proposition 5.4.4.3, p. 434. Definition A.2.6.3 and Remark A.2.6.4 give arbitrarily large sharply larger regular cardinals. Each endpoint is a small colimit of compact generators; bound the small family of index sizes and use Corollary 5.3.4.15.

proof.text: By [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], choose an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ and an essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ of $\lambda$-compact generators under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. For each endpoint $e$ of an arrow in $S$, choose one such presentation $p_e:I_e\to\mathcal G$ with colimit $e$. There are only a small family of endpoints (index them by $S\times\{0,1\}$, allowing repetitions), and each $I_e$ is small. The disjoint union of their sets of nondegenerate simplices is small. Choose an infinite cardinal $\theta\in\mathcal U$ at least $\lambda$ and at least the cardinality of that disjoint union. If $S$ is empty take $\theta=\lambda$. These choices concern only a small family, not all objects of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Definition 5.5.0.1 and Proposition 5.4.2.2(3); endpoint-size bound in the cardinal choice before Lemma 5.5.4.14

proof.text:
Put $\eta=2^	heta$ and $\kappa=\eta^+$. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power], $	heta<\eta$ and $\eta^	heta=\eta$; by [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular], $\kappa$ is infinite regular. Thus $\lambda\leq	heta<\eta<\kappa$, and $\kappa$ is uncountable. For $\mu<\kappa$ one has $\mu\leq\eta$ by the definition of successor cardinal. For $
u<\lambda$ one has $
u\leq	heta$; inject the sets of functions first into functions with codomain of size $\eta$ and then extend across an injection of their domains into a set of size $	heta$, filling the remaining coordinates by one fixed element of $\eta$. Consequently $\mu^
u\leq\eta^	heta=\eta<\kappa$. This includes the edge cases: if $\mu=0$ and $
u>0$, the function set is empty, while if $\mu=0=
u$, it is a singleton, which embeds into the nonempty set of functions from a $	heta$-sized set to $\eta$. All these power sets and successors remain in $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.3, printed p. 819, explicit power-successor calculation

proof.text: Every small $\kappa$-filtered indexing quasicategory is $\lambda$-filtered: a $\lambda$-small test shape is $\kappa$-small, so the required cocone exists by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. The mapping-space functor of each $g\in\mathcal G$ already preserves all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; hence it preserves the smaller class of $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Thus each $g$ is $\kappa$-compact. Each $I_e$ is $\kappa$-small by the bound in Step 1 and $\theta<\kappa$. Since $\mathcal C$ is presentable it is locally small and admits all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] to $p_e$ to conclude that every endpoint $e$ is $\kappa$-compact.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 401; compactness monotonicity and the endpoint-presentation bound

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the replete full subcategory of all colimits in $\mathcal C$ of $\kappa$-small coherent diagrams with values in $\mathcal G$. These colimits exist by presentability. The bounded-colimit clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus] makes $\mathcal H$ essentially small: it requires only that $\mathcal C$ be locally small and $\mathcal G$ essentially small, both supplied in Step 1. By Step 3 its vertex objects are $\kappa$-compact, so [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] makes every object of $\mathcal H$ $\kappa$-compact. Equivalence does not change this property because the two represented mapping-space functors are naturally equivalent. The empty diagram is allowed and contributes the initial object.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p. 426, bounded small-colimit hull; Corollary 5.3.4.15

proof.text: Fix any $X\in\mathcal C$. Its $\lambda$-accessible presentation from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] is $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I p$ with $I$ small $\lambda$-filtered and $p$ valued in $\mathcal G$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset] with its cardinal equal to $\lambda$ (its ambient quasicategory $\mathcal C$ admits all small colimits by presentability): it gives a small poset $A$ in which every subset of cardinality less than $\lambda$, including the empty one, has an upper bound, and a coherent functor $u:N(A)\to I$ along which the colimiting cocone restricts to a colimiting cocone. Put $q=p\circ u:N(A)\to\mathcal G$; it has the same colimit cocone with apex $X$. Apply [lem-coef-sharp-filtered-poset-subsets] with $(\alpha,\beta)=(\lambda,\kappa)$, using the power bound of Step 2. Its poset $\mathscr B$ of $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered subsets of $A$ is small, $\kappa$-filtered in the upper-bound sense, and covers $A$. Its nerve is $\kappa$-filtered directly from the test-shape definition: the fewer than $\kappa$ vertices of a test shape land in a family with an upper bound, and the unique order arrows to this bound extend the whole map to a cocone. Each nerve $N(B)$ for $B\in\mathscr B$ is $\kappa$-small: its nondegenerate simplices are finite strict chains, and there are at most $\max(\aleph_0,|B|)$ finite strings when $B$ is infinite or finite. This bound is less than the uncountable $\kappa$; the finite-string estimate follows by induction from the infinite-square identity [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power].

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9 using Proposition 5.3.1.18 (5.3.1.16 in the numbering cited by lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset) and Lemma 5.4.2.8, printed pp. 386-387 and 425-426

proof.text: For each $B\in\mathscr B$, choose $X_B=\operatorname{colim}_{N(B)}q|_{N(B)}$, which belongs to $\mathcal H$ by Step 5. Every finite chain in $A$ lies in some $B$: its finite set of vertices lies in one of the filtered subsets by [lem-coef-sharp-filtered-poset-subsets]. Hence $N(A)=\bigcup_{B\in\mathscr B}N(B)$ as simplicial subsets. The poset $\mathscr B$ is nonempty and directed since it is $\kappa$-filtered. The statement of [lem-coef-directed-cover-colimit-assembly] applies to this cover and the specified cocones: $\mathcal C$ admits all small colimits, and it gives a coherent $N(\mathscr B)$-diagram $B\mapsto X_B$ whose cocone to $X$ is colimiting. Thus every object of $\mathcal C$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects of the essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal H$ of $\kappa$-compact objects. Together with local smallness and existence of all small colimits, this is precisely $\kappa$-accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. $\lambda$-accessibility was the choice in Step 1.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, last paragraph; Propositions 4.2.3.4 and 4.2.3.8 for coherent directed-cover assembly

proof.text: Let $x$ be any $\kappa$-compact object and use its presentation $x\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{B\in\mathscr B}X_B$ from Step 6. By [lem-coef-infinity-compact-stage-factorization], apply the identity clause with $\gamma=\kappa$: the indexing quasicategory is small and $\kappa$-filtered, so there are $i:x\to X_B$ and the cocone arrow $r:X_B\to x$ with $ri\simeq1_x$. Thus every $\kappa$-compact object lies in the homotopy retract closure of $\mathcal H$. By the retract clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus], that full retract closure is essentially small. A full subcategory of it has a small family of equivalence-class representatives (select the represented classes satisfying compactness), and $\mathcal C^\kappa$ is replete, so it is the full subcategory on all objects equivalent to one of these small-indexed representatives; [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory], applied in the locally small $\mathcal C$, makes $\mathcal C^\kappa$ essentially small. This counts all compact objects, not merely the chosen compact generators.
